text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:
- Swiss Federal Railways and Italy's Railway (FS) signed an agreement to establish a company for the coordination of goods transport between the two countries.
- Adolf Wirz, founder of Switzerland's Wirz Group, which includes 12 communications advising firms, died at the age of 92 in Zurich.

- Geberit International AG, a Swiss sanitary systems firm acquired by Britain's Doughty Hanson & Co. last spring, posted an 8.7 percent increase in turnover to 500.7 million Swiss francs for the first half of 1997.
- Bank Sarasin, a Basle-based private bank, told its shareholders that its first-half group profit jumped by 58.5 percent to 28.5 million Swiss francs compared to the same period in 1996.
- Shell, BP, Esso and Migrol raised the price of petrol by two centimes last weekend due to the stronger dollar and rising prices.
- Basle pharmaceuticals giant Novartis was granted permission to put its Alzheimer medication Exelon on the market in Switzerland.
- Buero Fuerrer Group registered a five percent rise in profit to 2.46 million Swiss francs for the fiscal year 1996/97 ended April.
- Tecan Group, a laboratory automisation technology company, posted a first-half sales increase of 35 percent to 58.9 million Swiss francs.

- Reuters received documents last Sunday from the U.S. National Archives that seem to prove again that the Vatican Bank made transactions with the Deutschen Reichsbank via Switzerland during World War Two.
